_what: Who held a leadership role in the 54th Parliament. Hand-written and sourced, not derived from the corpus.
_sources: Ministerial List to take effect 7 April 2026 — https://www.beehive.govt.nz/sites/default/files/2026-04/Ministerial%20List%20-%202%20April%202026%20(1).pdf
Party leaders / deputies — party sites and RNZ; see _changes_in_term for the ones that moved
Presiding officers — Speaker Gerry Brownlee (from 2023-12-05), Deputy Speaker Barbara Kuriger (from 2023-12-06)
_note: A SNAPSHOT, dated above, of the last ministerial list inside the Hansard corpus (which ends 2026-05-28). Roles that changed earlier in the term are listed under _changes_in_term but are NOT in `roles` — so an MP who was a minister in 2023 and a backbencher by 2026 counts as a backbencher here, even though the scorecard averages their whole term. Update `_as_at` and the entries together.
_changes_in_term: 2023-11-27: government changed. Labour's 2023 ministers (incl. Grant Robertson, Ayesha Verrall, Ginny Andersen, Jan Tinetti, Megan Woods, David Parker, Kelvin Davis, Willie Jackson, Peeni Henare, Damien O'Connor, Priyanca Radhakrishnan, Barbara Edmonds, Willow-Jean Prime) held warrants until then and are not listed.
2024-03-10: Chlöe Swarbrick replaced James Shaw as Green co-leader.
2025-05-31: David Seymour replaced Winston Peters as Deputy Prime Minister (coalition rotation).
2026-04-07: Judith Collins and Shane Reti left the ministry in this reshuffle; Chris Penk and Penny Simmonds entered Cabinet.
2026-06-28: Nicole McKee replaced Brooke van Velden as ACT deputy leader — AFTER the corpus ends, so van Velden is the deputy for the whole scored period.

_tiers.leader: Party leader, co-leader or deputy leader; the PM and Deputy PM; the Speaker and Deputy Speaker.
_tiers.minister: Holds a ministerial warrant (in or outside Cabinet) or is a Parliamentary Under-Secretary.
